items.title: LC 11: Container With Most Water
items.text: Goal: find two lines that hold the most water. area = (right - left) * min(height[left], height[right]). How to derive it: (1) Brute force checks every pair, O(n^2). (2) The shorter line limits the water, however tall the other one is. (3) Start with pointers at both ends for the maximum width. (4) Compute the area and update maxArea. (5) Move the pointer at the shorter line inward: if height[left] < height[right], left++, otherwise right--. (6) Repeat until left >= right. Why move the shorter line: moving the taller one only shrinks the width while the shorter line still limits the height, so it cannot improve the area. Moving the shorter one gives a chance to find a taller boundary. Complexity: O(n) time, O(1) space. Remember: identify what limits the answer, then eliminate the possibilities that cannot improve it.
items.status: Your own write-up from 25 Oct. How the solve went (independent, hinted or solution seen) has not been reported, so no solve is logged.
items.check: Explain why moving the shorter pointer can never miss the best pair. Then solve it cold in C++ in 20 minutes.

items.title: LC 713: Subarray Product Less Than K
items.text: Your mistake: count++ when the product is below k. Correct: count += right - left + 1. After shrinking, the window [left, right] is valid, so every subarray that ends at right and starts anywhere from left to right is valid too. That is right - left + 1 new subarrays. Use this when counting subarrays and the condition stays true when the window gets smaller (all positive numbers here). It does not apply to exactly-K counts (use atMost(K) - atMost(K-1)) or arrays with negatives.
items.status: Hinted on 24 Oct, so this is a recipe, not a solve.
items.check: Explain why count += right - left + 1 counts each subarray exactly once, and why k <= 1 returns 0. Then solve it cold in C++ in 25 minutes.

items.title: *max_element: what it returns and how to use it
items.text: max_element(v.begin(), v.end()) is in <algorithm>. It returns an ITERATOR (like a pointer) to the largest element, not the value. Put * in front to get the value: int hi = *max_element(piles.begin(), piles.end()); For piles = [3, 6, 7, 11], the iterator points at 11 and * gives 11. Index of the max: it - v.begin(). Why an iterator: (1) you get the position as well as the value; (2) on an empty range it returns v.end() (not found), so never dereference that; (3) the same function works for every container. Mistake to avoid: int hi = max_element(...) without * does not compile. Siblings that also return iterators: min_element, find, lower_bound, upper_bound. For a few literal values, max({a, b, c}) returns the value directly.

items.title: Ceiling division (pile + k - 1) / k, and LC 875 Koko Eating Bananas
items.text: Goal: ceil(pile / k) using integers. C++ int division rounds DOWN (7 / 3 = 2), but 7 bananas at 3 per hour takes 3 hours. Logic: write pile = q*k + r, where 0 <= r < k. We need q hours if r = 0 and q + 1 hours if r > 0. (pile + k - 1) / k = q + (r + k - 1) / k. If r = 0: (k - 1) / k = 0, so the total is q. If r >= 1: k <= r + k - 1 <= 2k - 2 < 2k, so this part is exactly 1 and the total is q + 1. Intuition: k - 1 is the largest amount you can add without pushing an exact multiple past the next multiple; any leftover gets pushed over. Examples with k = 3: pile 6 gives 2, pile 7 gives 3, pile 8 gives 3, pile 9 gives 3. It is a calculator (always equals the ceiling), not a condition to satisfy. Overflow: write (p + (long long)k - 1) / k. LC 875 use: search speed k in [1, max(piles)] (at max speed each pile takes 1 hour, and h >= n). canFinish(k) = sum of ceil(pile / k) over ALL piles <= h, with the sum in long long (it can reach about 1e13). The predicate is monotonic, F F F T T T, so find the first T: if canFinish(mid), set ans = mid and hi = mid - 1; else lo = mid + 1. O(n log M) time, O(1) space.
items.status: Your notes from 30 Oct. LC 875 solution was seen (R-28 failed); cold re-solve due Sun 1 Nov.
items.check: Prove why (pile + k - 1) / k rounds up, using q and r. Then solve LC 875 cold in 35 minutes.

standards.title: Daily floor
standards.text: Every planned day ends with a logged artifact: solution code or closed-book answers. No artifact leaves the day empty on the strip, and tomorrow does not advance.

standards.title: Hard timers
standards.text: Easy 20 minutes, medium 35, hard 50. At the cap the hint ladder opens: pattern name, then invariant, then approach. Any hint makes the solve not independent.

standards.title: Re-solve rule
standards.text: A failed, hinted or solution-seen problem is re-solved cold 48 hours, 7 days and 21 days later. Every independent unseen solve returns once in a mixed set about 14 days later. Two independent cold passes close a problem.

standards.title: Quotas
standards.text: Tier 1 DSA patterns: at least 5 (usually 6 to 8) unseen mediums Accepted independently within 35 minutes, plus an unnamed mixed set and a mock before Interview ready. A new pattern opens only when the previous pattern's quota for that week is met or its retests are scheduled.

standards.title: Hard stop
standards.text: No timed solve or closed-book test after 00:30 IST. Work past it is practice only and is not logged as evidence.

standards.title: What independent means
standards.text: The code is Accepted by the judge with no hint, no AI and no outside help. Written invariants and edge cases are not required (your decision, 28 Oct).

standards.title: No AI in tests
standards.text: Timed solves, retests and closed-book answers are unaided. A solve done with AI is void and logged as void.

standards.title: Overdue retests block
standards.text: An overdue retest stops new material until it is passed or turned into a written remediation plan.

standards.title: Checkpoints cannot be skipped
standards.text: A failed checkpoint freezes new topics in the failed area for the following week. Remediation replaces them.

standards.title: Missed days
standards.text: No extra hours beyond the 43-hour week to catch up. Tier 1 quotas are never reduced: if they are not met by the gate, the gate moves (fallback mid-January), and Tier 2 depth is cut first.

standards.title: Stories
standards.text: Real incidents you can verify. No metric unless you measured it.

standards: Never move a due date (especially an overdue one) without your explicit permission.
